claims.text: Components inside a Pulumi package inherit the package's version; a package is the unit of versioning and distribution.
A source-based plugin package is distributed as source code in a Git repository, and its version is the Git tag on that repository.
Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow: apply a semver Git tag, then run `pulumi package publish`.
`pulumi package publish` sends package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.

Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing to the Private Registry; source-based packages referenced from a Pulumi.yaml can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit), even if not a valid semantic version.
Executable-based plugin packages are distributed as pre-built plugin binaries with per-language SDKs published to feeds (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, Go module proxy, or private equivalents).
An executable-based package's version is the version embedded in the published binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can publish executable-based packages to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
A repository should contain exactly one Pulumi package; Pulumi recommends this regardless of package type.
A repository containing multiple packages must either release them in lockstep or invent per-package release tooling that fights how Pulumi consumes packages.
Multiple components inside a single package are fine and ship together at the package's version.
The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with supporting components to secure and operate it.
One PulumiPlugin.yaml at the repository root defines the package.
Using a single monorepo with one giant package for all components is not recommended by Pulumi because it forfeits meaningful semantic versioning.
When unrelated components share a package, every package release versions every component the same way, violating semver.
Link targets exist: Private Registry concept page, pulumi_package_publish CLI page, packaging-components anchors, publishing-packages guide.
